_about: Mars overlay, deep-merged over data/events.json. Solar flares and moonquakes stay on the Moon (null removes them). Types: rules/types.ts EventsFile, rules/marsTypes.ts DustStormSpec.

duststorm._note: Rules track (M3), placeholders. One regional storm per mission (rules/storm.ts): it starts at a random time in sols 4 to 7 (180-360 s), is forecast one sol (60 s) ahead, blows for 2 sols (120 s), building up and dying down over 10 s. At full strength solar income is a third and night freezing is halved.
duststorm.source: 2018 Mars global dust storm: Opportunity's solar power fell from about 645 Wh per sol (early June) to 22 Wh on June 10 (The Planetary Society, planetary.org/articles/06-mer-update-opportunity-dust-storm-sleep); the dust also absorbs heat and narrows the rover's temperature swings (NASA JPL, jpl.nasa.gov/news/opportunity-hunkers-down-during-dust-storm). Forecasts like MRO's MARCI weekly Mars weather reports (Malin Space Science Systems, msss.com).

dustdevil._note: Dust devils (Mars M8, MS8; Owner B, provisional, for Chieri's review; starting values). Rules: rules/dust.ts scheduleDustDevils, placeDustDevil. One devil in each run of everySols sols, on a random sol of the run, so on average one every 3 sols (3 per mission, a fourth one time in three). By day only: it forms 8 to 24 s after a sunrise (around midday, when real dust devils peak) and stands for lifeSeconds, so it is gone before sunset (45 s). It moves in a straight line at speedMps (about the ambient wind) and passes the rover's position at its forming time, halfway through its life, at a random distance up to maxPassM (MS8: within 300 m of the rover). rampSeconds, radiusM and heightM are for the renderer. Cleaning and sensing distances: tuning.dust.
dustdevil.source: Perseverance's MEDA weather sensors counted about four whirlwinds per sol at Jezero, over a quarter of them dusty (Newman et al. 2022, Science Advances); dust devils form in the daytime heat, most often around midday (timing to check before it reaches text). A cleaning event around sol 420 (March 2005) sharply raised Spirit's solar output (NASA Photojournal, Solar Panel Dust Accumulation and Cleanings).
